cases.title: Double-click on the DP1 downpipe circle opens the CE Edit source window
cases.expected: A double-click on the outer circle of a freshly placed downpipe (tag DP1) opens CE's 'Edit source' window with DP1 in its Tag box, and not AutoCAD's Enhanced Attribute Editor. Cancel closes it.
cases.why_not_unit: Unit tests passed while the real AutoCAD double-click still reached EATTEDIT with nothing picked (BUG-859 round 1); only a real mouse double-click on a real block shows which window opens.
not_automated: The name of the Tag box in the Edit source window is not proven (the window has never opened); the check 'control Tag value DP1' uses the name 'Tag' and may need that one word corrected once the fix is installed.
The red centre, the angled DP text and the green label (BUG-860) are not clicked here; only the outer circle named in the bug.

cases.title: A finished CE command writes one outcome line to the CE log
cases.expected: CDCHECKCURRENT (the drawing check) runs without a window or a question, and the Civil CE log gains exactly one line 'Command outcome: CDCHECKCURRENT completed <n> ms' while it runs.
cases.why_not_unit: The line is written by the installed plugin when a real AutoCAD command ends; only a live run shows it reaches the log file that the log watcher reads.
not_automated: The 'cancelled' word is recorded by case R09 (the DP command ended by Esc) and the 'refused' case is recorded by R10 (CDCHECKIGNORE with its switch off); neither word is judged, because BUG-862 says today's words are wrong for both.

cases.title: The Settings window opens, Cancel closes it, and Tim's four settings files are unchanged
cases.expected: CDS opens 'Creative Engineering | Settings (CDS)' with the tabs Drafting, Pipes and Pits, Design, Survey, Display, Advanced, Newer tools and Fixes, a Cancel and a Save button, and the line 'No changes. Everything shown is saved.'; Cancel closes it; the four settings files have the same SHA-256 as before the window was opened (checked BEFORE the guard's restore runs).
cases.why_not_unit: The window loads Tim's real settings file in real AutoCAD; only a live run shows that opening it and pressing Cancel writes nothing.
not_automated: Changing a value and pressing Cancel (spec C14) and the per-tab look (C13): this case proves open, read, Cancel and unchanged files only.

cases.title: CDCHECKIGNORE with the switch off says so in one line and changes nothing
cases.expected: With the switch off, typing CDCHECKIGNORE prints 'Ignoring a finding is switched off in CE Settings. Nothing was changed.' at once, asks no question, and leaves no window or prompt behind; the four settings files are unchanged.
cases.why_not_unit: The refusal depends on the switch value CE read from Tim's real settings file when AutoCAD started, and on the real command line showing the one line with no question after it.
not_automated: The 'Command outcome' word for this refusal is recorded, not judged: BUG-862 says it is logged 'completed' and should say 'refused'. BUG-863 (the project record being saved on the off path) is not checked here.
The switch is read from Tim's file as it is (off). The ON paths of CDCHECKIGNORE (spec C17 to C19) need a settings profile and are not in this case.

cases.title: A new pipe joins the only pit at its end
cases.expected: CD draws a pipe from the new pit P8; the command line says 'Inserted flow arrow. Flow: P8 -> Open end' and 'End is free: open end flagged, connect it later.' once (the far end is free by design); the pipe's first vertex lies inside the pit's catch reach; the line never says the flow starts from an open end (the BUG-560 drift).
cases.why_not_unit: The join is made by the live CD point landing against the real pit in the drawing.
not_automated: Pit Schedule row P8 shows outlet IL 18.000 and the pipe's diameter (D03 assertion 3): the runner cannot read the Pit Schedule rows yet. Not part of this case.
The pit outline is not read. The catch reach is approximated as a circle of 641 mm around the pit insertion point (half the 600 x 900 default pit diagonal 541 mm plus the 100 mm catch).

cases.title: PIT and CD keep placing until Esc, and Esc keeps what was placed
cases.expected: After PIT and CD each places one object and offers the next, the command line says so; each Esc ends it with the 'Stopped' line and keeps what was placed (one new pit at 150000,-80000, at least one new pipe polyline, texts and arrow); no second New Pit or New Pipe window opens after an Esc; ONE U takes away the new pipe, its IL texts and its arrow and leaves the pit; the Civil log holds one outcome line for PIT and one for CD (the word is recorded, not judged: BUG-862).
cases.why_not_unit: The run is a chain of real AutoCAD command instances queued one behind another. Only live AutoCAD shows the next prompt, the Esc ending and what U takes back.
not_automated: Exactly one new pipe object: the composition of the new objects (how many polylines, blocks, texts) has never been read, so it is recorded here and only 'at least one' is asserted.
The 'Command outcome' words for PIT and CD are recorded, not judged (BUG-862: Esc-ended placements log 'cancelled').

cases.title: CE never saves the drawing: the file stays unchanged until the drafter saves
cases.expected: After placing a pit and a pipe and running CDSYNC, CDRECOVERINVERTS and opening and closing PITSCHEDULE, the drawing file on disk has the same SHA-256 and last-written time as when AutoCAD opened it, and the only new files beside it are CE's own _PRE_C7_ backups.
cases.why_not_unit: Only the real file on disk after a real AutoCAD session shows whether anything wrote to it.
not_automated: This case runs AFTER R01 has undone its pipe (U must be the last undoable command in R01), so CDSYNC and CDRECOVERINVERTS work on the fixture drawing itself; the checks only prove they ran and that the file on disk did not change.
CDREBUILD wording 'it does not save the drawing itself' (D18 assertion 2): CDREBUILD was dropped from this case because it has never been driven and its prompts are unknown.
